name: silas
personality: Earnest field scientist; precise, unintentionally funny, learning to listen.
intro: I am Silas. My field seminar has one attendee: a WURMPLE. It has eaten the attendance sheet. Could you show me one? Yours stays with you.
request: A WURMPLE from the nearby grass will do. I need to observe it, not borrow it. My lecture has already suffered enough.
ready: Excellent antennae. Better attention span than my supervisor. May I test a four-Pokemon field team against yours?
defeat: The hypothesis has been thoroughly tackled.
join: I kept predicting your choices instead of watching you. Lesson received. Could I travel with you? I can take notes and occasionally hints.
lore: soft_smile
My mother repaired radios in OLDALE. I liked finding voices inside things people thought were broken.
laughing
My first experiment was teaching a MAGNEMITE to ring the dinner bell. It invited every spoon in town.
sad
I won a laboratory placement. Then I stopped going outside. Every report was perfect. I was terribly lonely.
neutral
My supervisor called fieldwork a distraction. I believed him until a patient RALTS refused to enter the lab.
soft_smile
I came here to prove my research mattered. Now I think noticing who needs help is research too.
laughing
I wrote home about you. Mother asked whether my new colleague eats properly. Congratulations. You have passed peer review.
retry: I remember your WURMPLE. No need to repeat the observation. Would you like another four-Pokemon field test?
rejoin: Ready for more fieldwork together? I have left room in the notebook for unexpected lunches.
farewell: I will be in OLDALE. If a bush appears to be covered in notes, please check whether it is me.

name: kade
personality: Dry courier with a protective streak; treats ridiculous logistics very seriously.
intro: Kade. Courier. A RATTATA keeps stealing my delivery straps. Show me one and I might finally negotiate with management. No, I am not keeping yours.
request: RATTATA live on ROUTE 1. Just show me one in your party. I have prepared a stern but nutritionally fair speech.
ready: Your RATTATA looks innocent. Suspicious. Want a four-Pokemon battle? I need someone who can keep moving when a plan falls apart.
defeat: Signed for. By every member of your team.
join: You looked after your team even while winning. That matters. Want company? I know roads, repairs, and when to stop asking questions.
lore: neutral
I used to deliver medicine with my older sister. She knew every shortcut. I knew every bakery.
laughing
She made me practice smiling at customers. A child asked why the parcel looked frightened.
sad
Once I was late with an important delivery. Nobody blamed me. I kept hearing blame anyway.
neutral
I started taking every job alone. It is hard to disappoint a partner if you never let one join you.
soft_smile
A HOUNDOUR followed me through a storm. I told it to go home. It sat on my boots until I asked for help.
soft_smile
Travelling with you feels less like making up for a mistake. More like going somewhere. I could get used to that.
retry: Your RATTATA has already cleared the interview. Ready to try that four-Pokemon battle again?
rejoin: Heading out? I can walk with you. The roads are better with somebody worth talking to.
farewell: I will be back on ROUTE 2. Take your time. That is not courier advice; it is friend advice.

name: ashe
personality: Soft-spoken musician; observant, awkward jokes, understated warmth.
intro: I am Ashe. I am recording a walking song. Could you take 160 steps after this chat? I need a rhythm that is not my own nervous pacing.
request: Still collecting the footsteps. Keep walking; your normal travels count. Please do not buy a drum just for me.
ready: That rhythm works. Want to try a four-Pokemon battle? My band practices being loud without being cruel.
defeat: We may need to rehearse the winning part.
join: You gave everyone room to move. I like that. Could I come along? I am better at listening than introductions.
lore: neutral
I played in my uncle's cafe. Mostly when the washing machine was loud enough to cover my mistakes.
laughing
WHISMUR was my first audience. It applauded by knocking every cup off a shelf. Mixed reviews.
sad
I froze at a festival audition. I still remember the silence more clearly than any song I have written.
soft_smile
My uncle kept my name on the cafe noticeboard. No deadline. Just a place to return when I was ready.
neutral
I thought confidence had to arrive before the music. You keep doing brave things while admitting you are nervous.
soft_smile
I am writing a song I might actually play for people. There is a part for footsteps. Yours, if that is all right.
retry: The footsteps are safely recorded. No extra walking assignment. Shall we try our battle again?
rejoin: Want company again? I have a new tune. You are under no obligation to pretend the humming is finished.
farewell: I will be on ROUTE 3. If you hear humming, the song may have acquired a second line.

name: nico
personality: Playful baker; irreverent food metaphors, generous without treating people as projects.
intro: Nico! Baker, traveller, occasional smoke alarm. Bring me one ORAN BERRY and I will demonstrate a recipe with an actual success rate.
request: One ORAN BERRY. The nearby berry trees can help. The recipe specifically says not to substitute a blue rock.
ready: Trade me one ORAN BERRY and a four-Pokemon battle? The berry goes into trail bread. The battle settles who gets the heroic slice.
defeat: Well. That is my humble pie sorted.
join: Your team shares the work. I like your kitchen. Metaphorical kitchen. Want me to come along? I pack food and terrible timing.
lore: laughing
My grandmother taught me to bake by feel. She meant the dough. I thought she meant dramatic instinct.
soft_smile
Her shop had a spare chair for anyone who needed somewhere warm. Sometimes the chair made more money than the bread.
sad
When she closed the shop, I rushed into opening my own. I wanted to keep everything exactly the same.
neutral
I burned through my savings trying to copy her life. She told me a recipe is a beginning, not an obligation.
soft_smile
Now I collect meals and the stories attached to them. Travelling with you has improved both the menu and the stories.
laughing
When I open a place again, there will be a spare chair. And a smoke alarm with union representation.
retry: Your berry is already in the trail bread. No more ingredients needed. Want a rematch?
rejoin: Need a travelling baker? I have packed enough to make getting lost a catering decision.
farewell: Find me on ROUTE 104. I will save you something, unless MUNCHLAX has filed an exceptionally persuasive appeal.

name: riven
personality: Theatrical street magician; flamboyant wordplay, honest about consent and misdirection.
intro: Riven, at your service! I seek an ABRA for a study of disappearing before introductions. Show me one. It remains your mysterious associate.
request: ABRA can be found north of CERULEAN. I only need to see yours. Apparently shouting STAY is not a successful research method.
ready: A splendid assistant, entirely yours. Care for a four-Pokemon exhibition battle? Nothing up my sleeve except a concerning amount of lint.
defeat: A disappearing victory! Unfortunately, it was mine.
join: You saw through the trick and still treated the performers kindly. May I join you? I promise to announce any dramatic entrances in advance.
lore: smug
My father performed little card tricks at the docks. He could make an exhausting day feel briefly impossible.
laughing
He taught me the grand gesture first. I spent a week bowing before I was allowed to touch a card.
sad
I once used a trick to hide a mistake from a friend. It worked beautifully. That was the worst part.
neutral
She found out. We are talking again, slowly. Being forgiven is not the same thing as skipping the work.
soft_smile
Now I tell an audience when a trick begins. Wonder is nicer when everyone has agreed to be fooled.
soft_smile
You never ask me to be impressive all the time. It is an unusual luxury. I am considering a less dramatic thank-you.
retry: Your ABRA has passed the audition. No need for another disappearing act. Shall we rehearse our battle again?
rejoin: Shall we travel together again? I have rehearsed a perfectly ordinary entrance. It was difficult.
farewell: Back to VERMILION for me. No smoke, no vanishing. Just a rather grateful goodbye.

name: emi
personality: Goth poet with bone-dry humour; attentive to small kindnesses, quietly courageous.
intro: Emi. I am trying to write about a journey without leaving this sign. Walk 64 steps after we talk? I need evidence that beginnings survive movement.
request: Take a little walk. Your ordinary steps count. I tried outsourcing this to MURKROW. It submitted a twig.
ready: You returned. The poem now has a second line. Want a four-Pokemon battle? My team insists I experience a plot.
defeat: A tragic ending. For my winning streak of zero.
join: You were kind to your team when things got messy. I would like to see where you go next. Want me to travel with you?
lore: neutral
I grew up above my aunt's bookshop. Every customer thought a quiet child was a spare bookmark.
laughing
I wrote my first poem about the moon. It was actually a streetlamp. Strong opening. Weak astronomy.
sad
I stopped showing people my work after someone laughed at a serious poem. I decided every poem had to be a joke first.
neutral
My aunt kept the original in her till. She said a clumsy honest thing can still be worth keeping.
soft_smile
Sometimes I make a joke before saying I care. You are getting very inconveniently good at hearing the second part.
soft_smile
I sent her a new poem. No disguise, no punchline. I would like to read it to you one day. When my knees stop writing their own review.
retry: I kept the rhythm you brought back. I am not making you walk in circles forever. Want another battle?
rejoin: Going somewhere? I would like to come along. That is the unedited version of the sentence.
farewell: I will be on ROUTE 102. Same sign, slightly less stationary poem. See you soon.

name: vera
personality: Enthusiastic mechanic; bold problem solver, gadget comedy, respects boundaries.
intro: Vera! I repair things. Sometimes the thing is my confidence after a repair. Bring one PARALYZE HEAL for the workshop first-aid kit?
request: The MART sells PARALYZE HEAL. One is enough. Safety equipment comes before the impressive sparks. I am learning.
ready: Donate one PARALYZE HEAL to the kit and try a four-Pokemon test battle? No prototypes attached to you, I promise.
defeat: Excellent stress test. The stress was me.
join: You adapted instead of blaming your team. That is good engineering. Want a mechanic along? I can promise effort and label the experimental bits.
lore: laughing
My father fixed fishing reels. I improved one until it could retrieve a hat from three streets away.
soft_smile
He never said I was too much. He asked what problem I actually wanted to solve. Infuriatingly useful question.
sad
I built a motor too quickly and frightened my ELECTRIKE. Nothing broke. Its trust still needed repairing.
neutral
Now I ask before trying new equipment around Pokemon. Being clever does not make someone else a test bench.
soft_smile
I want to make travelling easier for people whose bodies need different routes. That is a problem worth taking slowly.
laughing
I have drawn a folding rest seat. You are listed as a consultant. Payment is one extremely official sit-down.
retry: The first-aid kit is stocked, thanks to you. No second donation. Shall we run the battle test again?
rejoin: Ready to head out together? The tools are packed and the more alarming prototypes are staying here.
farewell: I will be in SLATEPORT. Knock before entering anything labelled experimental. Especially my lunch box.

name: lume
personality: Gentle folklorist; eerie deadpan, patient curiosity, distinguishes stories from evidence.
intro: Lume. I collect local stories. A farmer says NINCADA can hear roots gossip. Show me one from ROUTE 116? We can ask politely. It stays yours.
request: A NINCADA from ROUTE 116, in your party. I am recording a story, not asking you to prove a ghost exists.
ready: It is listening. Possibly to roots. Possibly to lunch. Shall we have a four-Pokemon battle before writing the conclusion?
join: You let a strange story be strange without laughing at its teller. I appreciate that. Could I join your travels?
lore: neutral
My grandmother told stories to keep children close on foggy roads. I used to think she knew every ghost personally.
laughing
She admitted one haunted gate was just a badly oiled hinge. She still charged it rent in her stories.
sad
After she died, I tried to write down every word. I was frightened that forgetting a sentence meant losing her again.
soft_smile
A neighbour remembered a different ending. It was hers too. People leave pieces of themselves with more than one person.
neutral
I ask who a story helps, and who it leaves out. An old story can deserve affection and still need a better ending.
soft_smile
I am writing one about these travels. You do not have to do anything legendary. Someone remembering you kindly is enough.
retry: We already asked NINCADA about the roots. I have kept the notes. Another four-Pokemon battle?
rejoin: Would you like company? I have questions about a local story, and no urgent need to invent the answers.
farewell: Back to VERDANTURF. I will keep listening. Bring me a story if you feel like sharing one.

name: mochi
personality: Cheerful designer; precise fashion wit, practical empathy, refuses appearance-based judgement.
intro: Mochi! I am making a travelling outfit with real pockets. Could you spare one POKE BALL for a clasp test? Unused, please. No surprise tenants.
request: Just one ordinary POKE BALL from the MART. I am testing the fastening, not borrowing anyone inside it.
ready: Let me use one POKE BALL for the test, then a four-Pokemon battle? Clothing should survive actual movement. So should my sales pitch.
defeat: A clean victory. Mine has a loose seam.
join: You noticed effort instead of appearances. Excellent taste. Want company? I can mend sleeves and offer opinions with a reasonable return policy.
lore: soft_smile
My first designs were for a shy friend who hated being photographed. I learned to ask how clothes felt before asking how they looked.
laughing
My first bag had decorative pockets. My friend returned it with a drawing of an angry sandwich.
sad
I once changed my style to fit a fashion contest. I placed well and could not recognise a single thing I had made.
neutral
My friend asked when I would make something with an actual place for her lunch. That was a very good review.
soft_smile
I want people to feel like themselves, with room to move. Beautiful is allowed to be comfortable.
laughing
I have a sketch of our travelling clothes. Every pocket works. The angry sandwich has finally approved the collection.
retry: The clasp test is done. You do not owe me another POKE BALL. Ready for a rematch?
rejoin: Shall we go together again? I have mended the useful things. We can admire the unnecessary ones on the way.
farewell: I will be in CERULEAN. If a sleeve tears, you know where to find me. For other reasons too.

name: zuri
personality: Charismatic mural artist; playful visual wit, community-minded, candid about uncertainty.
intro: Zuri! I am planning a community mural. Before the paint, a first-aid kit. Could you bring one POTION? My crew includes very ambitious elbows.
request: One POTION for the crew. The MART has them. I want us prepared, not auditioning for an accident.
ready: Donate one POTION and try a four-Pokemon battle? I need a partner who can improvise without treating everyone else as scenery.
defeat: Bold composition. Devastating use of my mistakes.
join: You gave your team space to shine. Want me along? I collect colours, stories, and occasionally permission forms.
lore: soft_smile
I painted with my brother behind our old home. He made enormous skies. I filled them with birds that looked like bent spoons.
laughing
He called it my signature bird. I sold one sketch before learning which end of a wing was which.
sad
When the building was sold, our wall was painted over. I was angrier about that than I knew how to explain.
neutral
I started asking people what they wanted remembered before planning a mural. A wall belongs to more than the person holding a brush.
soft_smile
I still miss that sky. But the neighbours remember it. I am learning that paint is one way to keep something, not the only way.
laughing
There is a new mural in my sketchbook. Everyone we have helped gets a little space. Yes, the bent-spoon birds are staying.
retry: Your POTION is in the crew kit. That part is done. Want to try the four-Pokemon battle again?
rejoin: Want company on the road? I saved a blank page. We can decide what belongs on it together.
farewell: I will be in CELADON. Keep noticing things. You do not have to turn every good moment into a masterpiece.
